en: Salute that best of gurus, the venerable Kujeśa-Bhairava, by whom this mandala was truly brought together: at the edge of the Saṃvarta-mandala, he whose power of bliss is established in the sequential steps is most formidable; he has now united the first tetrad, the pentad situated in Akula and Kula, another hexad, four [units], another pentad, and again four principles. 1.1.
On the slopes of the glorious Himavat, situated within the peaks of Trikūṭa,
located in the midst of the city of Santāna, he whose form possesses many aspects.
It is indeed triangular, of threefold nature, blazing with the three powers and the three qualities;
it has the light of the moon and sun, and the intensely radiant splendor of fire.
It is divine, encircled by the three junctions of day and night, endowed with a triple-walled enclosure and the three paths,
provided with three gatekeepers, and equipped with three doors and bolts.
It was illuminated by many jewels, adorned with gardens and groves,
endowed with the qualities of spring, and filled with constant bliss.
There is a divine world of continua, frequented by both divine and non-divine beings;
therein resides that eternal Lord of the Worlds, who is both manifest and unmanifest.
For a short time, out of consideration for the relationship between cause and effect,
Bhairavīśāna remains motionless, having taken up silence.
There, all the hosts of gods, together with the kinnaras and mahoragas,
having gathered nearby, raised a tumultuous clamor.
Hearing the tumultuous noise, he asked, "Who are you, and why have you come here?
Himavat, with a serene mind, replied, "Let us go in search of him."
As soon as he beheld him standing there through the vision of Śiva-knowledge,
he saw the illustrious Lord arrive at my hermitage.
Having gone quickly with diligence to where the blessed Lord was staying with his family, Himavat spoke these words as a divine hymn of praise. (Kubjika Tantra 1.11)
Today my birth has become fruitful; today my ascetic toil has become fruitful;
today my station has become fruitful; my life has become fruitful.
Today I am blessed and my purpose is fulfilled; today my life's journey has borne fruit;
today the entire three worlds, with all that is moving and unmoving, have become fruitful for me.
O Protector, because my head is marked by your two feet,
I shall become one whose fame is renowned throughout the three worlds.
"O Lord of Gods, by your grace I shall attain omniscience; is this not sufficient, that the Master himself has come here? (Kubjika-tantra 1.15)
"What shall we do? What is my course? O Lord, let an instruction be given.
Having heard this lamentation of Himavat along with his family, [the Lord spoke].
The Blessed Lord, the Protector, smiling, spoke these auspicious words:
"O Mountain Himavat, well done! I am pleased with your devotion."
"O Himavat, O highly wise one, ask for some boon; we shall grant whatever is desired by your mind. I am truly satisfied with you. (Kubjika Tantra 1.18)
Himavat said:
"O Maheśāna, O Lord, what has been done for me by your own compassion?
O Lord of Gods, do what is pleasing [to you]. Thus spoke Himavat.
Having heard what was uttered by the mountain, the Lord of the Gods spoke these divine words, prepared to grant a boon with a gracious voice. (Kubjika Tantra 1.20)
First of all, whoever shall recite these five verses to you with diligence,
we shall certainly remain present for him by our own power.
A second time, I shall be present at your sacrifice;
and a third time, O wielder of the discus, you shall hold the sovereignty over all mountains.
"The fourth is my equality; the fifth bestows liberation upon men.
Thus, O Himavat, these five boons have been granted to you; speak again."
Himavat said:
"O Mahādeva, what need is there for anything else? You have indeed made me equal to yourself; so what further use is there for another thing? But rather, O God, grant me freedom from fear."
"Speak further whatever else pleases your mind;
I shall grant all of that, even though it was already mentioned by me previously. (KubjT 1.25)
Himavat said:
"Since there is no lack of anything anywhere in this hermitage, there is indeed no need for a servant;
however, there Dikkarikā shall perform the smearing of my body."
And since she is engaged in the practice of Dharma, let that be done by you, O Lord;
for that maiden Kālikā is dear to me, O Lord of Gods.
Thus it came to pass; therefore, remaining there, she who was endowed with virtue propitiated the Lord of Gods in many ways through humility and other such qualities.
Having approached with humility and having offered various kinds of praises and hymns over a long period of time, the Lord of the Family spoke thus to Kālī: *Kubjikātantra 1.29*
"I am pleased with you, Kālikā; tell me whatever is desired by your mind.
Whatever has been held in your heart, pray for it indeed without hesitation."
Having attained the state of being beloved and casting aside all shame, she spoke with a longing mind:
"O Lord, you are our protector, you who are worshipped by the gods."
Having thus heard these words arising from bliss, Maheśāna then quickly fulfilled that which was radiant with the qualities of the bliss of his command.
Mounted upon the seat of command, impelled by the infinite Śambhu,
he was shown everything in its entirety, the entire scope of the prior lineage.
Then the Mistress of the Kula, her being awakened, spoke thus:
"Everything has been shown to me; what wonder is there, O Lord of the Earth? (Kubjikāmata 1.34)
"O Lord, everything within the scope of action and its causes is known to me;
therefore, O Lord of Kujā, please explain that by which this is indeed accomplished."
O Supreme Lord, through your command, excellence and sovereignty have been born within me;
tell me, in accordance with the ultimate truth, the true essence of the meaning of this tantra.
O Lord of Kujā, if you are pleased, tell me everything in detail regarding your sixfold sacrifice, which has been observed by us in its entirety.
"O Lord, having understood the true nature of qualities, speak of the arising of those qualities,
so that I may behold everything in its entirety through the gateway of your command."
The existence of past events, that which was heard in previous recitations, and the exposition of the meaning of former kalpas have been made known and revealed by you. (Kubjika-tantra 1.39)
"O Lord, the great arising of the qualities of command previously shown has now resulted in ruin due to its loss; therefore, explain the matter clearly."
"O Lord, in age after age,
the mantra, tantra, ritual, and yoga practices have been taught by you in many ways for the sake of the compendium, yet they have not been fully grasped."
Now, O Lord, tell us of the power of that from which all this— the great arising of the qualities of sovereign knowledge— manifests clearly in its entirety.
Ānanda, Āvali, Prabhū, Yogin,
Atīta, and Pāda— how do these six types exist?
The illustrious Bhairava said:
"Excellent, excellent, O highly fortunate one, bestower of great bliss! The question you have asked is most wonderful and free from all defect."
Though this Siddhakrama, which is beyond conventional conduct, has been guarded by all the Rudras, the Vīras, and the Bhairavas, I shall nevertheless explain it to you.
Having come down through the sequence of the path of the Siddhas and established within the lineage of the Siddhas,
that which was concealed in all paths has today been revealed to you.
"O Goddess, I was previously incited by you, and you were incited by me in turn;
in this present aeon, I shall give you [myself] to you, and you, in turn, shall give yourself to me."
The ascetic woman did not realize that she was propitiating the Lord of Gods;
then, with a divine voice filled with joy,
the god began a celestial hymn of praise that awakens the understanding of all meanings.

Thus, by means of the correct ritual procedure, the power of Rudra was created by Svayambhū from the letters born of his own limbs, consisting of the nature of the phonemes from *na* to *pha*. (Kubjika-tantra 1.71)
The Goddess, composed of all syllables and marked by all auspicious characteristics,
arose with great majesty and stood facing Bhairava.
Mālinī said: "Who are you? I am a god; why have I come here?
O Goddess, how is it that you do not know me? By whom were you created?"
"O beloved, you were brought forth by me for the purpose of the descent [of the Lord] through the play of creation; tell me, O Bhairava, by whom were you yourself brought forth? KubjT_1.74.
"I am the mass of all colors, O blessed lady, the self-existent Lord of the world;
by means of the seeds produced from my own body, you were brought forth by me."
Therefore, you are praised as Rudra’s power under the name Vīrāvalī;
Mālinī, enraged by the arrows born from her own body, speaks thus.
"I have been produced by you through the phonemes; take back your own phonemes here, having extended the garland of phonemes which has the form of reality as its essential nature."

Having become the body of the primordial seed, with the nectar-circling serpent (amṛtakuṇḍalī) fallen asleep, from where have all the phonemes departed? Thus the Lord of the Gods is one whose mind is bewildered.
Overcome by supreme wonder, he reflected for a single moment;
then all those [elements], becoming agitated, dissolved into the principle of the individual soul (jīvatattva).
"Aho! Such is the power of the Goddess!"—with such a thought, the Lord of the World praised Bhuvanamālinī with various hymns.
Dark-hued, she who has entered the city of Kāmarūpa itself, who is Jikā at the seat of Jāla, divided into six parts, and who resides in the triple-pathed place at the central seat as Śṛṅgātakārā;

she whose limbs are embraced by the Siddhas, surrounded by sixty groups of clever yogis, and who is born of the *ḍa-ra-la-ka-sa-ha* [syllables] within the heart-lotus—may that Śakti of Rudra protect me!
Thus ends the first chapter, titled "The Descent of Candradvīpa," in the *Śrīkubjikāmata*, according to the tradition of the Kulālikas.
The venerable Bhairava said: Victory to you, O Goddess Mālinī, stainless one who destroys all impurity!
O Goddess, you are the power of knowledge, the sovereign; you are intellect, the increaser of splendor.
The mother of all beings, established in this saṃsāra, is the goddess Mātā Vīrāvalī; O compassionate one, show mercy, O affectionate one! KubjT_2.2.

Victory to you, O Supreme Power of Knowledge! You are born from the splendor of the ultimate reality of Nirvāṇa; you have emerged in manifest form as the Supreme One, yet you are again the straight line of Will and Action, like a sleeping lord of serpents.
(3) You are the Lord whose form is like a coil, the radiant power of Sound (nāda-śakti);
you are praised as the luminous one, the beautiful one, the auspicious one, and by the names Jyeṣṭhā, Vāmā, Raudrī, and Ambikā who is beyond mind (manākhyā).
(5) You are the nature of the Bindu, the Avadhūtā, the shape of the half-moon, the triangle, and the letters A, U, Ma, and I.

(6) Joined with the letter *e*, you attain oneness; you abide in the form of the *bhaga* as the very essence of reality (*tattva*). (7) Born from the primordial reality, you are the womb-form that awakens Śrīkaṇṭha and is the mother of Rudra.
(8) Likewise, you possess infinite power, are most subtle, and are the one who receives the offering (*argha*) for the three forms (*trimūrti*), namely Amarīśa and Bhārabhūti.

(9) She whose essence is the lord of the lunar days (*tithīśa*), who has become a pillar (*sthāṇubhūtā*), and is named Hara; she who consists of Jhaṇṭīśa, Bhauktīśa, and Sadyojāta; she who is worshipped by Anugraheśa; (10) she who enjoys union with Mahāsena during the company of the cruel;
(11) she who is the nectar at the end of the sixteen [vowels], whose body is flooded by the flow of the mass of the Bindu, and who is the entirety of perfect supreme bliss.

(12) O Bestower of the bliss of Nirvāṇa, Bhairavī, attached to the play in the garden of Bhairava; (13) Supreme Mālinī, worshipped by the garland of Rudras, the power of Rudra, Khagī, Siddhayogeśvarī;
(14) Mother of the Siddhas, the All-pervasive One, the Mass of Sounds, the Ocean of the Source-syllables, you are Vāgviśuddhā, the Mistress of Speech.
(15) You are Mātṛkā, Siddhā, Icchā, Kriyā, Maṅgalā, Siddhalakṣmī, Vibhūti, Subhūti, Gati, Śāśvatā, Khyāti, Nārāyaṇī, Raktacaṇḍā, Karālekṣaṇā, Bhīmarūpā,
Mahocchuṣmā, Yāgapriyā, Jayantī, Ajitā, and Rudrasammohanī.
(18) You, the goddess Navātmā, are seated upon the lap of [your consort];

(19) you are worshipped, O Goddess, by ministers who follow the path of mantra, who are devoted to the drinking of heroes (*vīrapāna*), and who are deeply faithful; (20) with the five nectars (*pañcāmṛta*) and festivals of divine drink, [you are honored] by those of one birth and those of two births.
O you who delight in wine and meat, you are gratified by those men born of three, four, five, six, or seven lifetimes— by those auspicious yet trivial beings,
and by those shaven-headed Kāpālikas who proclaim their spells, sciences, and vows, and who carry skeletons as ornaments.

(24) By practitioners (*sādhaka*) and spiritual sons (*putraka*), who have ascended to the divine conduct, who utter these mantra-syllables— namely, the prostrations (*namaskāra*), *oṃ*, *svāhā*, *svadhā*, *vauṣaṭ*, *vaṣaṭ*, *phaṭ*, and *hūṃ*— and who hold rosaries of beads in their left hands while reciting them; (25–26) by these [practitioners].

(27) O Goddess, you who bestow the yogic accomplishments (*yogasiddhi*) upon yogins, you are worshipped by the Mothers, by those initiated into the mandala, and by groups of yogins and yoginīs gathered in assembly; (28–29) and you look with eyes like lotus petals, filled with affection, upon him who is intent on the play of Rudra.

(30) For him, there exists unimpeded accomplishment (*siddhi*) that dwells in heaven and the intermediate space, reaching down to the seven netherworlds and extending to the sky-dwellers. (31) Whoever, being pure, recites this *daṇḍaka* once, twice, or thrice a day with devotion, and whoever always remembers it— (32) even such a person [is protected] from weapons, fire, thieves, and the ocean.

(33) O Goddess Mahālakṣmī, out of affection for your son, you protect even on the mountain peak those who are thieves of gold, those attached to the wives of others, and those defiled by great sins such as being slayers of Brahmins or slayers of cows;
(34–35) remembering your face which resembles the full moon, O Goddess, they are set free.
(36) With their cheeks rubbed by excellent earrings of shimmering *māṇikya* gems,
(37) even those who have been bound with firm bonds, with serpent-nooses, and with their feet shackled to their arms— (38) even they are released, O Goddess, through the chanting of your name.

(39) Having called to mind your two lotus-feet amidst terrible and great diseases, O Mahākālī, whose splendor is like the fire of cosmic destruction, you are served by Skanda, Govinda, Brahmā, Indra, the Moon, and the Sun, and by the flower-armed god [Kāmadeva], who are tawny like the filaments of the lotuses upon the garlands on their crowns and the swarms of bees.
(42) O Mother of all heroes, Bhairavī! I have come to you, Bhairava, for refuge.
(43) Forgive my transgression, forgive my transgression, O Śivā!
Thus was the Great Goddess praised by the high-souled Bhairava.
Then, having burst through the *liṅga*, the Supreme Goddess emerged.
Resembling blue collyrium in appearance, she was humpbacked and pot-bellied;
her face was slightly grimacing, and her hair was coarse and standing erect.
Beautiful and yet deformed, possessing many forms and appearances, she who extended her left hand spoke thus to Vāmadevī: (Kubjika Tantra 2.5).
Pervaded by the bliss of realization and overwhelmed by the bliss of being praised,
I do not know who here praises me, who I am, or to whom I am granting a boon.
The Great Being spoke thus: "How was it that you endured my glance, which is as difficult to behold as a venomous serpent? (KubjT 2.7)
Then ask for whatever it is that pleases your heart.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
"O Great Goddess, for the sake of grace, grant me the favor of your command;
O Mother Kujā, by your fierce austerity, my own power has been diminished."
"O Queen, this has arisen because of that; this was previously spoken by me.
Having heard this, the Great Queen, filled with shame, looked at him with faltering eyes. (KubjT 2.10)
"What has been accomplished by you, O Mahādeva, that we have been put to shame?"
The illustrious Bhairava said: "I have previously told you this regarding the scope of the command and the observance (*ājñāsamaya*).
Having first favored those who are equal to me, you shall thereafter become the Mother of the Gaṇas (*gaṇāmbikā*)."
Whose is this lineage of the Siddhas, which has come down through a succession of transmission—from me to you, and from you back to me? (Kubjikātantra 2.13)
Having heard those terrifying words, the Goddess turned her face away;
out of shame and impetuous emotion, she assumed the form of Kubjikā. (Kubjikātantra 2.14)
"But why do you feel shame, O Queen? Previously, I gave you my command;
now, give it to me quickly. Let there be no hesitation, let there be no delay. (KubjT 2.15)
The venerable Kubjikā said: "O Lord of Kubjā, when something is uttered impulsively by one who is unawakened and intoxicated,
is it proper to apply a sense of restraint toward that?"
The illustrious Bhairava said:
O Goddess who bestows grace upon all, do you not perceive this within yourself?
Nothing exists anywhere that is devoid of me, nor anything that is devoid of you.
O Mistress of the Gods, through the union of our mutual qualities and the connection between cause and effect, you are my guru; I am yours—of this there is no doubt.
This command belongs to Rudra, Bhairava, and the Vīras, and it is not for anyone else;
if you do not regard the disciple as a friend, then bestow [the teaching] upon him.
When the Goddess spoke thus, he said: "O Lord, all this shall come to pass;
however, this was done at the end, devoid of its preceding portion."
"O Lord, my mind is not inclined to abandon the delightful island of Candra;
meanwhile, you should cultivate the final of all paths."
"This path of the Western Tradition bestows everything upon the perfected ones (siddhas);
I shall go once again there, to the Kulaparvata in Bhārata."
He described to those who know it Śrīparvata, known as Kumāra, adorned with a parasol of shadow, from the beginningless past until the end of time.
Having spoken thus, she quickly went to the glorious Kaumāraparvata;
there dwelt the goddess Chāyātmikā, who is unmanifest yet possesses a manifest form.
Having spent the course of time, as far as he might look toward the directions,
he saw that entire great forest of Liṅgapūrṇa in the north.
Eighty yojanas in length and circular all around,
it is provided with four gates and surrounded by tens of millions of sacred fords (tīrtha).
It was crowded with many perfected beings (siddhas), delightful to the mind, and incomparable;
it was filled with a multitude of qualities of darkness (tamas) and teeming with many wonders.
By the falling glance of the Goddess, prosperity suddenly arrived;
therefore, Śrīśaila was designated by the name of the Goddess as "the Unestablished."
The line drawn by his thumb at that very spot became a divine river, serving as the boundary for both sides.
Having rendered its shadow motionless and having bestowed the command of Śambhu, [he said]:
"Whoever enters here shall become equal to me."
He is the destroyer and the creator, independent, the illuminator of fallen knowledge;
his command and sovereignty extend throughout the three worlds, including all that is mobile and immobile.
Having thus incited him, she went to Mount Trikūṭa;
having spent her time there, she favored the one named Kiṣkindhā.
And having bestowed upon him the power of his command and favored the Rākṣasas, he said:
"By this means, I shall remain on the shore of the ocean free from fear. (KubjT 2.33)
Having gone there to Kanyākumārī, you waited for the turn of time;
then, after favoring the ocean, you went again to Daradaṇḍī.
There, the goddess Chāyādharī, with a mind of unmanifest qualities,
shall again release her command for the sake of benefiting the worlds.
"Whatever words were spoken in the former place shall come to pass right here.
Having said this, she departed for the distant western Himalayan caverns.
There stands a small forest grove named Olambikā,
where women clad in red garments, themselves red, dwelling in red, are eager for pleasure.
Remaining there, situated within the abyss, dwelling in the depths of the cave,
for as long as time endures, the entire world consists of the yogin.
Having been satisfied by them through manifold means of policy and stratagem, the goddess Kujjeśvarī, serene and profound, then spoke this: KubjT_2.39.
Because that which is composed of manifold methods and endowed with the quality of discernment was cast down by his two feet, it is therefore called Oḍḍiyāna.
Having come from the circle of sky-farers (khecarīcakra) by the grace of the unfailing command, it will become as it was before, a locus of eight times ten million virtues.
"You shall have eight mind-born sons endowed with the six qualities;
you are the mother of the eight Śākinīs and the sovereign of the eight lion-thrones."
Rudrāṇī, Rudraśākī, Gomukhī, Sumukhī,
Vānarī, Kekarī, Kālarātrī, and Bhaṭṭikā.
Vāmana, Harṣaṇa, the mighty Siṃhavaktra,
Mahākāla, Ekavīra, Bhairava, and Pracaṇḍaka.
The four-armed leader of the Gaṇas, the elephant-faced one of great ferocity, Airāvata, and Vināyaka—these six are the attendants. (Kubjika-tantra 2.45)
Accompanied by eight sons and daughters, she abides in cessation (nivṛtti) and is the regulator;
he is the creator of many emanations and is radiant with perfectly complete qualities.
And when the Kṛta age has arrived, O Uḍḍamaheśānī, Mitrānanda shall be your husband;
eight sons will exercise authority in the Western lineage.
The six lords of the families will exercise authority;
in age after age they shall arise, appearing through the succession of their distinct designations.
Thus everything has been indicated to you: the flood of transmissions (kramaugha) and the Kula path.
O future Raktacāmuṇḍā, we shall go wherever we desire.
Having thus granted them the boon, she returned to Karāla,
which was ablaze with a great mass of flames and possessed the radiance of a fire of blazing splendor.
The most wonderful splendor of the Goddess, consisting of a mass of great flames, was held by him;
therefore, his majesty is known by the name Jāla.
After some time, radiant with awakened rays,
she beholds before her a manifold variety of diverse arrangements like a magical illusion.
Whose divine creation was this that previously existed here at the sacrifice?
By the power of my splendor, you were cast down and did not flee.
O you with the terrifying face, who spreads the net of illusion,
the sovereignty over Jālandhara shall be yours before long.
Having come from the wheel of the sky-farers (khecarīcakra), the Lord Śrī Siddhakauṇḍalīśvara,
the master who knows all things, shall become your protector.
Ten daughters named Karālī will be born to you;
these ten, known as Uttarānandā, will be most excellent in their qualities.
But there will be six attendants, O auspicious lady, in the range of the followers: Ājñā, Ānanda, Samatā, Ekattva, Karālī, and Duhitājanā. (Kubjikātantra 2.57)
Mālā, Śivā, Durgā, Pāvanī, Harṣaṇī,
Jayā, Suprabhā, Prabhā, Caṇḍā, and Rugmiṇī.
Śakuni, Sumati, Nanda, Gopāla, Pitāmaha,
Pallava, Meghanirghoṣa, Śikhivaktra, and Mahādhvaja.
Kālakūṭa—these ten sons shall be the lords of the throne;
from Meghavarṇa onwards, they will be your hosts in this world.
Bṛhatkukṣi, Ekadaṃṣṭra, Gaṇeśa, Vighnarāj, Prabhu,
and Mahānanda— these six shall become the lords of the Gaṇas.
The lords will bring about the supreme bliss in age after age;
however, at the conclusion of the decline of knowledge, they will repeatedly produce various distinctions of terminology.
"Karālī shall be born in your lineage by my command.
Having spoken thus, the Great Goddess departed for the great forest of Sahya.
Filling the three worlds with the rays of her full orb,
she pervades the entire universe without exception, extending as far as the Lokāloka mountain.
For as long as that state persists through various means and methods,
for that long Caṇḍākṣī performs powerful service in manifold ways.
Performing many arrangements for ease through various means,
they blaze with rays of splendor, filled with the qualities of Caṇḍākṣī.
On that mountain where the Goddess remained, her radiance blazing like a thick, radiant flame,
that region became stable, while everything else, both moving and unmoving, was consumed by fire.
At the end of time, the Mother, her eyes filled with joy, beholds this entire mountain, which is filled with manifold structures and other wonders.
And at that moment, Amitatejas beheld Caṇḍākṣiṇī before him,
filling [the world] with universal nectars and longing for the qualities of the divine stream.
The Great Goddess said this: "Well done, O you whose desires are fulfilled!
Since this place has been filled by you, you are truly one whose form is complete."
This mountain, from which you have arisen, shall possess sovereign power through the conjunction of the equinox,
by virtue of this [place] having been consecrated by you.
Therefore, you shall indeed become the Mistress of the Seat (Pīṭheśvarī) in age after age;
your seat is the mass of splendor, and you are the one authorized until the end of the Dvāpara age.
"In this world, Cakrānanda will certainly become your husband;
he will be the Lord of the Kula, the support of the scriptures, with a form like a full mandala."
There will be exactly twelve young maidens for you in this existence;
from among them, each one shall have ten million subordinate officials under their authority.
Likewise, there will be sons and half-brothers who,
impelled by my command, shall come from the circle of sky-farers.
By which name I shall address you, since I have been inspired with faith by you:
Haṃsāvalī, Sutārā, Harṣā, Vāṇī, and Sulocanā.
Mahānandā, Sunandā, Koṭarākṣī, Vṛkānanā,
Yaśovatī, Viśālākṣī, Sundarī, and likewise the twelfth, [Dvādaśī].
In their sovereignty over the lion-throne on Mount Pūrṇa, they are the noble maidens;
likewise Vali, Nanda, Daśagrīva, Hayagrīva, and Hayas.
Sugrīva, Gopati, Bhīṣma, Śikhaṇḍin, Khaṇḍala,
as well as Śakra, Caṇḍādhipa, and the Siddhas who bestow grace upon all.
They will be the revealers of the path beginning with the *haṃsabheda*;
namely, Āmoda, Pramoda, Sumukha, and likewise Durmukha.
"May there be no obstacles, and may those who create obstacles be protectors on your paths;
all this shall be according to the proper rule before you, O Caṇḍākṣī. (KubjT 2.81)
"He will remain unknown to me; let us go as we please.
Having spoken thus, she went quickly to where the auspicious river Ucchuṣmā flows.
Situated within the forest of Mahocchuṣma, it carries forth a multitude of divine and non-divine beings;
there, where the lake of Mahocchuṣma is, there also is the great lake Nīla.
There the goddess, endowed with the qualities of divine command, took her delight;
having sported for the duration of time, she remained upon both banks.
As soon as Viśvāṅgī beheld Tattvāṅgī,
she saw her radiant with the splendor of the springtime tilaka flower, yet displaying the haughty pride born of sensual enjoyments.
Seeing her who was flowing and streaming through the three worlds by her own will, the mother laughed and said: "Who are you, and from where have you come here?"
Seeing her, the mother was bewildered; though she knew [the truth], she acted as if she did not know.
